# All-length half-integer triangle chains: the low positive-normal sector

A shorter complete proof now appears in
`candidate dd382d5b121a0508`. It proves a
sharp universal arithmetic-envelope deficit bound and lists all thirteen
scalar polynomial coefficients needed for its verification. The present
three-variable certificate remains an independent complete route.

This note completes the other positive-normal sector for the restricted
class of half-integer symmetric common-vertex triangle chains. All
scalar certificates here are exact rational identities. General OC,
arbitrary nonsymmetric chains, and arbitrary continuous dimension are
not conclusions of this note.

## Theorem

Let T=conv(0,e_1,e_2), V=area(T)=1/2, and let the integer fibers at -h
and h+1 be r_h T, h=0,...,m, with

    r_0=R>0, R>=r_1>=...>=r_m>=0,
    r_(h-1)-r_h <= r_h-r_(h+1)  (1<=h<m).

For every a in [1/2,2/3] and beta>=0, the original closed cap

    -beta z+a x_1+(1-a)x_2 >= R/3

has at least 2/9 of the total mixed area. The selected point is the
single actual own centroid (0,R/3,R/3) in the base-zero triangle.

The exact affine-radius theorem in
`candidate a15fce1d462289cc` reduces
each proposed violating cap, without changing its center or normal,
to an affine radius profile. The high-sector theorem in
`candidate 77cefa95257c7b19`
proves the following two further reductions without using a>=2/3:

* If beta>=lambda/3 for the affine slope lambda, each left fiber alone
  pays its own centroid fraction 4/9, proving the target.
* Otherwise, after R=1 scaling, 0<k=lambda/R<=1 and 0<=beta<k/3.
  The two threshold/radius ratios increase along the affine leg, so
  a violating finite leg extends, with only nonpositive additional
  deficits, to the maximal leg r_h=(1-kh)>0.

Their proofs are elementary and reproduced in Steps 1 and 2 of the
high-sector note. They apply to every a considered here. The case of
no outer fibers, every zero terminal radius, and lambda=0 have already
been treated exactly in those reductions. It therefore suffices to
prove the remaining maximal-leg inequality for

    1/2<=a<2/3,  0<k<=1,  0<=beta<k/3.                   (1)

The endpoint a=2/3 also follows from the high-sector theorem.

## Lemma 1: convexity along the affine leg

Put c=1-a, t=1/3. Let F_r(u) be the normalized triangle tail, and
define for h>=0

    f_-(h)=F_(1-kh)(t-beta h),
    f_+(h)=F_(1-kh)(t+beta(h+1))                          (2)

on h<1/k, extending both functions by zero for h>=1/k. Both extended
functions are nonnegative, continuous, convex, and compactly supported.

Proof. On the positive-radius leg both thresholds are positive. Their
ratios to the radius increase by the derivative calculation in the
high-sector note. Hence either cap is empty before the radius reaches
zero, and the stated zero extension is exact. For 1/2<a<2/3 each
proper cap branch has one of the two formulas

    r^2-u^2/(ac),          (ar-u)^2/[a(2a-1)].             (3)

Under the affine substitution (2), the first quadratic has second
derivative 2[k^2-beta^2/(ac)]>0, since ac>=2/9 and beta<k/3.
The second quadratic has nonnegative second derivative because it
is a positive multiple of the square of an affine function. The
value and first derivative match at the proper-branch transition,
as follows directly by substituting u=cr in (3). At the empty-cap
transition the latter square has value and derivative zero. The
derivative is therefore nondecreasing on the whole half-line.

At a=1/2, the proper tail is (r^2-4u^2)_+. Its nonzero quadratic has
positive second derivative under (1). At its final knot r=2u, its
left derivative is -4u(k-2beta)<0 for the minus cap and
-4u(k+2beta)<0 for the plus cap, whereas the right derivative is
zero. Thus the derivative jumps upward, again proving convexity.

## Lemma 2: a combined integral and first-pair lower bound

Write

    J=sum_(h=0)^infinity [f_-(h)+f_+(h)],
    I=integral_0^infinity [f_-(x)+f_+(x)] dx,
    O=f_-(0)+f_+(0).

Then

    J >= (1-k)I+(1+k)O/2.                                (4)

Proof. Convexity and the trapezoid inequality on each unit interval
give J>=I+O/2, including truncation knots in interval interiors. The
first pair also gives J>=O. Multiply these unconditional inequalities
by 1-k and k, respectively, and add them. Both coefficients are
nonnegative by (1), and sum to one. This proves (4).

## Exact formulas for the integral and the first pair

Let

    L=c-t=2/3-a,       U=a-t=a-1/3,
    O_-=1-t^2/(ac).

In the strict range (1), both ak-beta and ck-beta are positive. The
left integral is

    I_-=[(a-t)^3/(3a(ak-beta))
                    -(c-t)^3/(3c(ck-beta))]/(2a-1).      (5)

The apparent a=1/2 singularity cancels identically. Its canceled form
has numerator

    27a^4k-54a^3k+36a^2k-9ak-beta+k

and denominator

    81a(a-1)(ak-beta)(ak+beta-k).

All denominators in this canceled form are nonzero for (1), including
a=1/2. The right contribution has the following three cases:

    Region 0: 0<=beta<=L,
      I_+=[(a-t-beta)^3/(3a(ak+beta))
                -(c-t-beta)^3/(3c(ck+beta))]/(2a-1),
      O_+=1-(t+beta)^2/(ac).

    Region 1: L<=beta<=U,
      I_+=(a-t-beta)^3/[3a(2a-1)(ak+beta)],
      O_+=(a-t-beta)^2/[a(2a-1)].

    Region 2: U<=beta,
      I_+=O_+=0.                                         (6)

These are obtained by integrating the exact upper-branch square and
subtracting the lower-branch square. Explicitly the identity for a
positive threshold is

    F_r(u)=[a/(2a-1)](r-u/a)_+^2
              -[c/(2a-1)](r-u/c)_+^2.

Each nonzero affine square integrates to its initial positive value
cubed divided by three times its slope. The left initial upper and
lower values are positive for a<2/3; the right lower one vanishes
at beta=L and the upper one at beta=U, giving exactly (6).

For region 0 the common factor 2a-1 cancels from the difference in
I_+, just as in (5). For region 1 set beta=L+(2a-1)v. Then
a-t-beta=(2a-1)(1-v), so every occurrence of 2a-1 cancels or remains
as a numerator factor. At a=1/2 this region shrinks to beta=1/6,
and I_+=O_+=0 exactly, as the direct equal-normal tail also shows.
Thus formulas (5)-(6), in their canceled forms, apply on the closed
normal endpoint a=1/2. They can alternatively be checked directly
using (r^2-4u^2)_+ there. Set I=I_-+I_+ and O=O_-+O_+.

## Lemma 3: the exact scalar inequality

For the parameters (1), with I and O given by (5)-(6),

    (1-k)I+(1+k)O/2
       >=(4/9)[1/(3k)+1/2+k/5].                          (7)

Proof by explicit rational polynomial certificates. Let H be the
left side minus the right side. The regions in (6) cover the entire
allowed range because beta<=k/3<=1/3. Parameterize them by a variable
v in [0,1] as follows:

    region 0: beta=L v,
    region 1: beta=L+(2a-1)v,
    region 2: beta=U+L v.

In every region set

    k=3beta+(1-3beta)w,  0<=w<=1.                        (8)

Every (1) is covered: beta<1/3 and the required value is
w=(k-3beta)/(1-3beta) in (0,1]. The extra parameter boundaries are
used only in the polynomial certificate.

After the indicated substitution and exact cancellation, write
H=N_j/D_j for each region j. The positive denominators can be
specified without any hidden sign evaluation. With the same mapped
beta and k as in (8), they are

    D_0=27*[810ac k(ak-beta)(ak+beta)(ck-beta)(ck+beta)],
    D_1=9*[810ac k(ak-beta)(ak+beta)(ck-beta)],
    D_2=[810ac k(ak-beta)(ck-beta)]/L.                    (9)

Every quantity in brackets is positive for (1); L>0 there. In the
third denominator the division by L cancels from its mapped factors,
so it is a polynomial in a,v,w. The numerators N_j are also explicit
polynomials, generated equivalently as the canceled products H D_j.
They are provided in full in the certificate JSON and reconstructed
from formulas (5)-(9) by the independent verifier.

Map a=1/2+x/6. The following boxes cover each complete v,w square.
On every box substitute v=v_0+(v_1-v_0)y and
w=w_0+(w_1-w_0)z and expand the numerator in the tensor Bernstein
basis of its displayed coordinate degrees:

    region   v interval    w interval     degrees      minimum coefficient
       0       [0,1]         [0,1]        (12,8,6)             0
       1       [0,1]         [1/2,1]      (10,7,5)             0
       1       [1/2,1]       [0,1/2]      (10,7,5)             0
       1       [0,1/2]       [0,1/2]      (10,7,5)             0
       2       [0,1]         [0,1]         (7,4,4)           21/128

Every coefficient is a nonnegative rational number. As the tensor
Bernstein basis is nonnegative and sums to one on its unit cube, all
three N_j are nonnegative on the whole stated parameter ranges.
The explicit coefficient reconstruction formula is

    c_(i,j,l)=sum_(p<=i,q<=j,r<=l) A_(p,q,r)
       binom(i,p)binom(j,q)binom(l,r)
       /[binom(n_1,p)binom(n_2,q)binom(n_3,r)],

where A_(p,q,r) are the mapped power coefficients and (n_1,n_2,n_3)
are the listed degrees. The full finite coefficient list, all three
raw numerators and denominators, and the parameter intervals appear
in `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/half-integer-affine-low-sector-bernstein-candidate.json`.
The exact construction is
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/certify_half_integer_affine_low_sector_candidate.py`; its historical
filename does not turn any numerical sampling into part of this proof.

Dividing N_j>=0 by (9) proves (7) throughout the required range (1).
There is no division by a vanishing denominator at the extra parameter
boundaries. The omitted beta=k/3 boundary is proved by the pairwise
argument, and a=2/3 by the high-sector theorem. Values at a=1/2 are
included by the canceled formulas as already justified.

## Completion and measure/center checks

The elementary finite-sum upper bound proved in Lemma 1 of the
high-sector note is

    sum_(h=0)^infinity (1-kh)_+^2 <=1/(3k)+1/2+k/5.

Combine this with (4) and (7). The original cap J is at least
(4/9) sum (1-kh)_+^2, exactly 2/9 of the total original even-chain
mass. This excludes a violating maximal affine leg, then a violating
finite affine prefix, then a violating arbitrary concave radius
profile by the two exact deficit reductions. This proves the theorem.

Every integral in the argument is an auxiliary one-variable estimate
for an explicitly convex cap-area function; it never replaces the
mixed-integer measure itself. Both original mixed masses remain exact
finite sums of triangle areas. The central fiber has positive area,
so q=2 and 0<H_2(S)<infinity. The chosen center never moves, all
integer bases stay integral, and the one original oblique beta is
shared by every term. A zero-radius terminal fiber has zero H_2 mass
in every closed ambient halfspace and is deleted without approximation.

Together with the high-sector theorem this settles every nonnegative
continuous normal (after exchanging its two coordinates). The
previously proved positive-normal reduction at the own centroid,
using the touching radius majorant r_h<=R, reduces every mixed-sign
or negative continuous normal to such a cap with no larger mass.
The paired-sign comparison reduces arbitrary integer tilts to -beta.
A purely vertical cap through base zero contains one full triangle
from every pair and therefore at least half the source mass. These
dependencies yield the exact own-centroid theorem for all closed
ambient halfspaces of this restricted half-integer symmetric class.
